_meta.description: HR employee records with injected salary outliers and missing survey scores. The salary column has 8 extreme values injected (5000, 8000, 500000, 750000) alongside a realistic normal distribution (mean ~85k, std ~22k). The IQR fence is [-17875, 189850], so 7 of the 8 injected values fall outside it and are flagged as outliers. performance_score and satisfaction_score have realistic survey non-response rates (10% and 7% respectively). The attrition column is 18% positive — a 4.68:1 class imbalance.
planted_issues: salary: 7 outliers beyond 3×IQR fence [-17875, 189850] — injected extreme values (5000, 8000, 500000, 750000)
tenure_years: 11 values above 3×IQR upper fence (14.4) — NOT a real defect, just the tail of a clipped exponential distribution. Legitimate long-tenure employees.

score.note: Two required warnings (salary outliers, performance_score nulls) and one borderline warning (satisfaction_score nulls). No critical issues. Expected score 58-82. Lower bound is 58 because borderline tenure_years outliers at the clip boundary can add extra deduction.

required_findings.note: 7 values are outside the 3×IQR fence (injected: 5000, 8000, 500000, 750000). The profile reports outlier_count=7 explicitly. These represent likely data entry errors or test records.
10% null rate — above the 5% warning threshold. Missing performance data creates bias risk in any downstream model.

optional_findings.note: 7% null rate — above the 5% threshold. Whether flagged as warning vs info depends on model judgement.

forbidden_severity_overrides.note: tenure outliers are at the natural clip boundary, not injected errors. If reported, must be info-level.

note_on_max: Two required + two optional legitimate issues = max 4 real findings. More than 6 suggests noise.
